extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, authors, and publishers (participants in scholarly publishing)
extracted.subtask_description: Ethical duties and standards for publishers, editors, reviewers and authors in primary research journals, covering conflicts of interest, peer review, confidentiality, authorship, data, image integrity, and related publication practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respectful and professional behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect staff, authors, reviewers, editors and readers to treat one another with respect and dignity; do not tolerate disrespectful, inappropriate or unprofessional behaviour, discrimination, harassment, bullying, or retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all participants; fosters trust in science and protects integrity of scholarly record. Unprofessional or abusive conduct is unacceptable in submissions, reviews, editorial communications, and interactions with staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardianship of the scholarly record (publisher duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher has responsibility to support editors and reviewers and ensure best practice is followed in publications; act as keeper of the 'minutes of science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher should provide policies and procedures, work with industry associations (STM, COPE), support investigations of misconduct, and take measures such as corrections, retractions, or expressions of concern when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard editorial independence (publisher duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure potential for advertising, reprint or other commercial revenue has no impact or influence on editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher must separate commercial considerations from editorial judgment; follow Elsevier's 'Editorial independence' policy to avoid conflict between revenue and content selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate to set industry best practice (publisher duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote best practice by offering editors membership of COPE and providing Crossref Similarity Check reports for submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with other publishers and industry bodies to set standards; provide tools and access to services that help detect misconduct and improve ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide editors with technical, procedural and legal support (publisher duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support editors in communications with other journals/publishers and provide specialised legal review and counsel if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher to assist editors during investigations, disputes, or legal issues and to provide systems and processes to enable ethical editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate researchers on publishing ethics (publisher duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide extensive education and advice on publishing ethics standards, especially for early career researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer training and educational content (e.g., Researcher Academy, PERK) to raise awareness of ethical requirements and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests for editors who are employees of the publisher
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors employed by Elsevier must report any competing or conflicting interests that could affect editorial judgement; report as they arise and via annual declaration; may be disclosed on journal website or papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing interests include financial and non-financial interests (employment, consultancies, affiliations, advisory roles, patents, travel grants, ownerships, directorships). Minor investments (<1% publicly traded stock) and pooled pension funds excluded. Elsevier employees are discouraged from submitting research to Elsevier journals (with narrow exceptions); any submission must disclose employment and ensure independent peer review. Editorial staff forbidden to use information acquired through work for personal gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication decisions (editor duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor is solely and independently responsible for deciding which submitted articles should be published; validation of the work and its importance should underwrite decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor may be guided by editorial board policies and constrained by legal requirements (libel, copyright, plagiarism). Editor may consult other editors, reviewers or society officers; must ensure decisions are based on intellectual content and importance to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure fair, unbiased, and timely peer review (editor duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor shall ensure peer review is fair, unbiased, and timely; research articles typically reviewed by at least two external and independent reviewers; seek additional opinions if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select suitably expert reviewers, avoid selection of fraudulent reviewers (follow WAME), review disclosures of conflicts and self-citation suggestions for potential bias; editors may edit or withhold reviews that don't follow policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection and avoidance of fraudulent reviewers (editor duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select reviewers with suitable expertise and follow best practice to avoid fraudulent peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use verification methods and follow WAME guidance to detect fabricated reviewers or identities. Ensure reviewer expertise matches manuscript subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair play and nondiscrimination in editorial evaluation (editor duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate manuscripts for intellectual content without regard to race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, ethnic origin, citizenship, or political philosophy of authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal policies should encourage transparency and honest reporting; ensure peer reviewers and authors understand expectations; use standard electronic submission systems and provide a transparent appeal mechanism for editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations and journal metrics (editor duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor must not attempt to influence journal rankings by artificially increasing any journal metric and must not require references to that (or any other) journal's articles except for genuine scholarly reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not coerce authors to cite editors' or reviewers' work or require citations to boost metrics. Editors may remove inappropriate suggested citations from reviewer comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial confidentiality (editor duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect confidentiality of all material submitted to the journal and all communications with reviewers unless otherwise agreed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except in open peer-review systems, protect reviewers' identities. In exceptional circumstances and in consultation with the publisher, limited information may be shared with other journals/institutions investigating misconduct. Do not use unpublished materials for personal research without express consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of generative AI in editorial process
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must follow the journal's generative AI policies for the editorial process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the generative AI policies for journals page for specifics; editors must comply with guidance on AI-assisted technologies when handling manuscripts and editorial tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of editorial competing interests (editor duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential editorial conflicts of interest should be declared to the publisher in writing prior to appointment and updated as new conflicts arise; publisher may publish such declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must not be involved in decisions about papers they authored, those by family members or colleagues, or those relating to products/services in which they have an interest; such submissions must be handled independently and disclosed in the published paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vigilance over the published record (editor duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor should work to safeguard the integrity of the published record by reviewing and assessing reported or suspected misconduct in conjunction with the publisher or society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include contacting authors, considering complaints, communicating with institutions, using publisher systems (e.g., plagiarism detection), and coordinating prompt publication of corrections, retractions, or expressions of concern when evidence of misconduct is convincing. Editors should stay up to date on policies and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to editorial decisions (reviewer duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review assists the editor in making editorial decisions and may assist authors in improving the paper; reviewers perform scientific evaluation and alert editors to ethical issues or substantial overlap with other work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should cite relevant prior work when stating that an observation or argument was previously reported. When writing reports, treat authors respectfully; unprofessional or biased reviews may be edited or withheld by editors. Decline review if unqualified or unable to review promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity and declaration of competing interests (reviewer duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be conducted objectively; personal criticism is inappropriate; declare potential conflicts before agreeing to review and discuss recusal with the editor if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of conflicts include collaborations with authors within previous three years, same institutional affiliation, or close personal relationships. Reviewers must consider whether such relationships could bias their review and recuse if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer citation recommendations (reviewer duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not suggest citations to their (or associates') work unless for genuine scientific reasons and must not recommend citations to increase citation counts or visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete bibliographic details and clear justification for suggested citations to enable editorial oversight. Editors may remove inappropriate citation suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidentiality (reviewer duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any manuscript received for review must be treated as confidential; reviewers must not share the review or information about the paper or contact authors without editor permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with the journal's AI policies in peer review. Co-reviewing or discussing with colleagues should be agreed with the editor first to preserve confidentiality and ensure proper credit. Do not use unpublished materials in your own research without explicit written consent from the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of generative AI in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must respect the journal's policy on the use of generative AI and AI-assisted technologies in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the generative AI policies for journals page for permitted/forbidden uses, disclosure requirements, and how AI use affects confidentiality and authorship of review content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting standards for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of original research should present an accurate account of the work performed and an objective discussion of its significance; data should be represented accurately and the paper should contain sufficient detail and references to permit replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fraudulent or knowingly inaccurate statements are unethical and unacceptable. Review and professional publication articles should be accurate and objective; opinion pieces should be clearly identified as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access and retention (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may be asked to provide research data for editorial review and/or to comply with open data requirements; be prepared to provide public access to data where practicable and to retain data for a reasonable number of years after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the journal's Guide for Authors for specific data policies. Failure to provide data when required may impede publication or trigger further inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and acknowledgement of sources (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should ensure their work is entirely original; when using others' work or words they must appropriately cite or quote and obtain permission where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give proper acknowledgement to others' work, cite publications that influenced the reported work. Do not use or report privately obtained information without explicit written permission. Plagiarism in all forms is unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple, redundant or concurrent publication (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should generally not publish the same research in more than one primary journal or submit the same manuscript to more than one journal concurrently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondary publication (e.g., translations, guidelines) can be justified only when conditions are met: agreement of journals, same data and interpretation, citation of the primary reference. See ICMJE for acceptable forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation practices (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must cite relevant, timely, and verified literature (generally peer-reviewed) to support claims and ensure statements relying on external sources are cited accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive or inappropriate self-citations or arrangements to cite others' work; avoid excessive citations to support a single statement. Use DOIs for persistent links. If authors suspect citation suggestions were made against policy, inform the editor or contact Elsevier Researcher Support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author confidentiality (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information obtained in the course of confidential services (e.g., refereeing manuscripts, grant applications) must not be used without explicit written permission of the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exploit privileged information gained through confidential processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria and responsibilities (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship should be limited to those who made significant contributions to conception, design, execution, or interpretation of the study; others who contributed substantively should be acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding author must ensure appropriate co-authors are included and have approved final version and submission. Changes to authorship after submission are exceptional and require agreement of all authors and editor review; Elsevier journals do not allow authorship changes after acceptance. All authors take collective responsibility for the work and each is accountable for accuracy/integrity of any part they are responsible for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of generative AI in scientific writing and figures (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must follow the journal's generative AI policies for use of AI and AI-assisted technologies in writing, figures, images and artwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit the generative AI policies for journals page for specifics on disclosure, permitted uses, and restrictions related to AI-generated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional claims: maps and institutional affiliations (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors choose how to designate territories and affiliations; Elsevier takes a neutral position on territorial disputes. Maps should show the area actually studied and not display larger areas than the study bounding box; include a note that map lines delineate study areas and do not necessarily depict accepted national boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may request map changes during review. Use full standard institutional titles or standard abbreviations so institutional names can be independently verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazards and human or animal subjects (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: If work involves chemicals, procedures or equipment with unusual hazards, the author must clearly identify these in the manuscript. If the work involves human participants or animal studies, follow Elsevier's Human Research and Animal Research policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ethical approvals, informed consent information or protocol identifiers as required by journal policies. Failure to comply may prevent publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of competing interests (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors should disclose any financial and personal relationships that could be viewed as inappropriately influencing their work; disclose all sources of financial support and role of sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include employment, consultancies, stock ownership, honoraria, paid testimony, patents, grants. Disclose at the earliest possible stage and state when funders had no role in design, analysis, writing, or decision to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of fundamental errors (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an author discovers a significant error or inaccuracy in their published work, they must promptly notify the editor or publisher and cooperate to retract or correct the paper if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the editor or publisher is informed by a third party of an error, authors must cooperate and provide requested evidence. Prompt notification and cooperation preserve integrity of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image integrity (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not acceptable to enhance, obscure, move, remove, or introduce a specific feature within an image; adjustments (brightness, contrast, color balance) are acceptable only if they do not obscure or eliminate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manipulation for clarity is permitted but manipulation for other purposes can be scientific ethical abuse. Authors should comply with journal-specific image policies (e.g., provide original images as supplementary material or deposit in a repository).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial transparency (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: For relevant journals, authors are expected to conform to industry best standards in clinical trial registration and presentation (e.g., CONSORT guidelines) as set out in journal policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register trials appropriately and follow reporting guidelines; journals may require trial registration numbers, protocol details, and adherence to CONSORT when applicable.
